clinician.final_diagnosis: ADEM, most likely triggered by a recent viral illness.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old male presented with decreased consciousness following a week of severe headaches, arthralgias, myalgias, visual disturbances, and light/sound sensitivity, initially diagnosed as URI/complex migraine. Upon current admission, he exhibited confusion, GCS 10/15, right eye swelling, tachycardia, decreased breath sounds, and signs of meningeal irritation. A follow-up brain MRI revealed newly developed T2-FLAIR signal intensities in the left hemisphere, right parietal, and temporal lobes, with mild leptomeningeal enhancement. CSF analysis showed elevated protein and lymphocytic pleocytosis, while PCR for viral pathogens (including HSV) and bacterial cultures were negative. He was diagnosed with ADEM and treated with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone, leading to significant improvement in consciousness and orientation within 3 days. Steroids were tapered over 4-6 weeks. At discharge, he had full orientation and marked improvement in cognitive and motor functions, able to perform ADLs independently, with mild residual fatigue and mood fluctuations. At 2-week follow-up, he remained clinically stable without recurrence of neurological symptoms.
